text:
maria: heads-up — saw a couple of weird rate/quota header shapes from the hosted api and the python client is currently dropping some of them when 429s happen. reproducible in my local testing.

kevin: ah, what headers are you seeing? sample?

maria: pasted curl output — this is from a canary model route. note mixed casing and a Retry-After that's an RFC1123 date: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2026 15:12:05 GMT
Retry-After: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 00:00:00 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 500
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1717000000
Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 1200
redwood-quota-reset-ms: 1717005000000
```

maria: the python client library currently normalizes header names to lower-case but also coerces numeric headers to ints with a strict parser which chokes on the RFC1123 Retry-After. result: SDK surfaces a "429" exception but no parsed retry info.

olivia: ugh, we've seen variants — Retry-After sometimes in seconds, sometimes a date string, and some customers have custom quota headers (redwood-*) with ms timestamps. we should robustly parse both.

sam: agreed. also the async client path misses the header-extraction hook entirely when streaming errors happen (we only attach headers on non-streaming responses). that's why some users can't implement client-side throttling.

kevin: proposal: add a helper util in devx package, e.g., `redwood.devx.rate_limit.parse_headers(headers)` that accepts a case-insensitive mapping and returns typed strings + numbers and a canonical `retry_after_seconds` int/None. API shape: 

```
# returned dict (conceptual)
{
  'limit': 'int | None',
  'remaining': 'int | None',
  'reset_ts': 'int | None',      # unix seconds
  'quota_remaining': 'int | None',
  'quota_reset_ts': 'int | None',
  'raw': { ... },
  'retry_after_seconds': 'int | None'
}
```

kevin: parsing rules: if Retry-After is digits -> seconds; if RFC1123 -> compute seconds from Date header if present, otherwise return None. Also accept ms fields (like redwood-quota-reset-ms). Fallback heuristics documented.

maria: that sounds perfect. also please make it fully typed (mypy-friendly) so our public sdk API surfaces stable TypedDict or dataclass. many users rely on static typing.

sam: implementation notes: both sync and async clients should call the same util. For streaming responses we already have the low-level socket reader; we can attach header extraction on first chunk if status >= 400. Might need small refactor.

olivia: small UX ask — expose a `RateLimitInfo` on the raised exception (e.g., `RedwoodAPIError.rate_limit_info`) so customers can do: `except RedwoodAPIError as e: backoff = e.rate_limit_info.retry_after_seconds or default_backoff`

kevin: +1 on exception attribute. We should also add a convenience backoff generator `redwood.devx.rate_limit.exponential_backoff(base=1.0, max=60.0, jitter=True)` so customers can combine server-provided retry_after with local policy.

devx-bot: deploy 2026-03-21T15:20:00Z :canary rate-limit-headers-parser v0.3.2 -> prod-canary (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

maria: i'll test the canary tomorrow morning US-PST with a script that pumps requests to the canary model.

sam: i'll open an issue and assign — will include: tests for RFC1123 parsing, ms header handling, typed return object, exception attribute, and streaming path hooks.

kevin: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/1298 — put design notes and example snippet for downstream usage. tagging @devex. :eyes:

olivia: tiny doc ask — examples in quickstart should show how to use `retry_after_seconds` + `exponential_backoff` to build respectful client-side throttling (sample code, 5-10 lines). keeps customer integrators from hammering.

maria: thanks all. i'll paste my test harness here once i've run the canary so we can add it to e2e suite. :+1:

kevin: thanks! moving to tracking board.
